heroHeadline: Von der Leyen Unveils European Heatwave Plan as EU Wildfire Total Passes 666,000 Hectares
heroSubtitle: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen used her State of the Union address in Strasbourg to call this year 'the summer of truth,' proposing a new European Heatwave Plan and a future EU firefighting aircraft fleet after a season she said burned roughly 660,000 hectares, caused 35,000+ heat-linked deaths and cost EU grain farmers about €2 billion. EFFIS separately put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 666,534 hectares as of 15 September, up ~7,115 hectares over two days — still well below 2025's record pace for this point in the season. No new wildfire outbreaks, fatalities or evacuations have been confirmed across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania since early September, and Cernavodă's reactors remain offline pending a Danube-flow reassessment.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
